newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Plutonium transport by air to rise - Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: Plutonium transport by air to rise - Greenpeace.

text.p: Transportation of plutonium by air has risen and is set to increase, resulting in the flight of large quantities of radio-active material over densely populated parts of Europe, Greenpeace International said on Monday.

"There's no safe way to transport plutonium, but by air has got to be the worst way. The drop test means that casks need only remain intact after a fall of nine metres according to new IEA standards," said spokesman Shaun Burnie.

In 1994, there was one flight of reprocessed nuclear fuel from the UK to Switzerland and, in 1995, three flights, Greenpeace said. So far this year, there have been three flights from Belgium to Scotland, it said.

Contracts between British Nuclear Fuels (BNFL) and utilities in Switzerland and Germany indicate a large increase in the number of so-called "nuclear flights" in the next two to five years, Greenpeace said.
"If BNFL intends to return all fuel to the client and return it by air...there will be another 40 flights to Switzerland and maybe 70 to Germany," said Burnie.
The traffic entails the shipment of spent nuclear fuel to BNFL sites in the UK for reprocessing and the return of the reprocessed plutonium fuel to the client.
